structured_output.what_is_happening: This token (1sMM…, non-pump address, pool opened directly on PumpSwap about 1 minute after the mint) copies the "NPCs" project from wenpc.family. That project is a pump.fun AI-agent concept: creator fees spawn LLM trading wallets that buy $NPC. The real project's site says "Buy on pump.fun" and links @wenpcfamily. The one that is working is 68SV…pump, at about $6.2M mcap and up about 12,800% on the day. In the last ~2.5 hours at least 8 other "NPCs" clones appeared with non-pump addresses or odd DEX setups. They showed large paper market caps ($2.5M–$4.3M), and every one now has $0 liquidity. One of them, a4h4…, had 1,762 buys against 227 sells before its liquidity went to zero. This token fits the same pattern: $1.5M of volume on a $120k cap within 45 minutes, 534 unique buyers against only 53 unique sellers, 45 GMGN bundler wallets holding about 20%, 0% of the LP locked with few LP providers, and liquidity larger than market cap. It looks like a liquidity-farm rug clone riding the real NPCs launch.

narrative.description: AI-agent 'NPCs' mechanism: creator fees on pump.fun spawn autonomous LLM trading wallets that reinvest into $NPC. It is a real, current narrative, and the canonical pump.fun token is at about $6M mcap.
narrative.why_spreading: A fresh AI-agent tokenomics gimmick whose canonical coin went up about 128x today. That attracts clone deployers who target buyers searching for the ticker.

token_connection.why_this_token: It only shares the name, ticker and metadata (description 'Created on https://wenpc.family', same X handle). It is not a pump.fun address, even though the official site says to buy on pump.fun.
token_connection.competing_tokens: 68SVgJMajJ7YvW8fMU23jdwxCkCoFmVKdKcLMQ8qpump ($6.2M mcap, $222k liquidity) is almost certainly the canonical token. Clones a4h4…, CZJN…, 3Vkm…, 6kgc…, JBVp…, BCvE… and GQZM… all show $0 liquidity. The unrelated Non-Playable Coin NPC is also large.

authenticity.evidence: About 10:1 unique buyers to sellers (534 vs 53), 8x hourly turnover, 45 bundler wallets, and 5,027 RugCheck holders against 477–607 on GeckoTerminal and GMGN (which suggests an inflated holder count). The GMGN image duplicate count is 5. Sibling clones on the same pattern (for example, many buys, few sells, then liquidity 0) have already rugged.
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not read X (402 error). Some buyers may be real people who confused this token with the canonical one.

structural_risks: 0% of the LP locked and few LP providers, so the deployer can pull liquidity at any time
Liquidity is larger than mcap, which suggests the deployer seeded the pool to extract it
Sibling clones with the same name already went to $0 liquidity within hours
Copycat of a canonical token that is 50x larger

structured_output.counterargument: Confused buyers are pouring money in: 171 unique buyers in 5 minutes, price up 70% in an hour, and no dev or sniper concentration in the top 10. If the deployer waits to pull, a spillover pump could 2x the price from $120k to $240k within the window. The canonical token did 128x, and its buyers may rotate into 'cheaper NPC' clones.
unknowns: Who controls the LP and when they will pull it
Whether wenpc.family or @wenpcfamily endorse any CA (the site shows a placeholder CA)
How the sibling clones' prices behaved before they rugged

structured_output.thesis: A non-canonical clone of the hot pump.fun NPCs AI-agent coin, with an unlocked LP and inflated, bundled volume, in a clone family whose siblings have all already gone to $0 liquidity. The most likely outcome is an LP pull well before any 2x.
